Hi David — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers we can include in the SIG packet; I've attached a one-page summary and a network diagram. Jonas will follow up with the log retention specifics for Dedicated.

Hosted (Redwood API, multi-tenant hosted):
- Description: Shared hosted environment where Redwood operates the inference runtime across our regional infrastructure. Customers access models via the Redwood API. Runtime and control plane are managed by Redwood; tenants are logically isolated at the project/account layer.
- Security implications: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest under Redwood's keys by default; SOC 2 controls cover operational procedures. No physical/dedicated hardware per customer. For regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private.
- Evidence: redwood_sig_hosting_summary.pdf, redwood_network_diagram_v3.png

Dedicated (reserved capacity in Redwood-managed pools):
- Description: Customer gets reserved GPU capacity isolated from other tenants at the scheduler/runtime level. Still operated by Redwood but with resource isolation and optional network segmentation.
- Security implications: Stronger isolation reduces cross-tenant attack surface; customers get predictable performance and can request tailored retention/ingress controls.
- Evidence: capacity_isolation_playbook.pdf (excerpt attached)

Private / VPC / On-prem:
- Description: Customers run the Redwood control plane in their VPC or deploy a private on-prem package. Full network and storage control sits with the customer; optional air-gapped installs available.
- Security implications: Customer-managed keys, KMS/HSM integrations, and the greatest control over egress and logging. Suitable for regulated workloads and data residency requirements.
- Evidence: private_deployment_architecture.pdf

I attached the one-page summary and the network diagram. Link to the SIG answers (editable): https://drive.redwood.com/sig-hosting-playbook?id=12345

> We're completing the SIG questionnaire for Acme's vendor review. A few items focused on hosting/deployment modes require a short plain-English explanation and any evidence we can attach:

Hi David — quick technical clarifications below and attached a worksheet we usually include in SIG responses.

Dedicated logs and retention (short):
- Where written: By default, application and audit logs for Dedicated are collected by Redwood's managed logging pipeline and stored in our encrypted object store (region-matched). For customers that require push-to-customer, we support log forwarding to customer-managed S3/Cloud Storage or a Syslog endpoint on request.
- Retention: Default retention for operational logs is 90 days; audit logs tied to SOC 2 evidence are retained 365 days. Retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private customers via support/contract.
- Access: Logs are accessible to authorized customer contacts via secure links or delivered via secure transfer; for Private/VPC on-prem deployments, logs remain under customer control.

SOC 2 mapping: Attached is the SOC2_SIG_mapping.xlsx which maps common SIG questions to our SOC 2 controls and evidence artifacts (control IDs, evidence filenames, audit dates).

Attachments:
- sig_answers_hosting_sheet.xlsx
